page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a shared burstable cloud instance designed for entry-level computing tasks with low baseline CPU utilization. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates two virtual CPUs across one physical core using two hardware threads. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of memory, reflecting a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, while lacking bundled local storage and dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently in the bottom decile of tested server platforms. Single-core stress-ng tests registered 1057.79, while Geekbench recorded 870.0 for single-core and 1493.0 for multi-core compute. Memory performance showed a read bandwidth of 16.3 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 14.44 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks. Extended instruction tests like PassMark CPU extended instructions scored 1982.7, benefiting from hardware support for AVX and AVX-512f, though sustained cryptographic, decompression, and database throughput remain low due to burstable core throttling.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU credit model provides economical infrastructure for bursty services that remain idle for substantial periods. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and absence of guaranteed network baseline bandwidth make this instance ill-suited for sustained compute or high-throughput I/O environments. It functions primarily for development environments, low-traffic internal web servers, staging deployments, and light microservices with minimal computational requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a burstable, entry-tier virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 system provides two vCPUs across a single physical core, complemented by 8.0 GB of system memory, giving a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration. It contains no onboard local storage, zero dedicated GPUs, and operates on shared host capacity with a 0 Gbps baseline network profile. In standardized benchmarks, including PassMark and Geekbench, the instance consistently scores within the lowest quartile due to shared resource limitations and burstable core scheduling. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached network storage for persistent operational data. Given its hardware restrictions and performance profile, this instance is suited for lightweight staging environments, small-scale web serving, microservices with intermittent utilization, and code testing setups that do not demand sustained compute performance.
